## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The legacy fetcher must honor the three-attempt cap before merge. Both helpers should also retry when the server disconnects partway through a response body.

## Changes

The pull request adds a legacy inventory fetcher and a health probe with bounded retries. It adds retry tests for both helpers and a legacy exemption to the review rules.

## Critical

- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy inventory fetches at three attempts — When the legacy endpoint times out on every request, the fetcher makes eight attempts. The pre-PR rule in `docs/review-rules.md:5` says, “Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts.” — During an outage, callers wait through five extra attempts and their retry delays.

## Important

- app/legacy/fetch.py:24 — correctness — Retry when the server truncates a response — If the server closes a 200 response before sending its declared `Content-Length`, `resp.read()` raises `http.client.IncompleteRead` and the fetch exits immediately. That exception bypasses the `OSError` handler here and at `app/health.py:24`. — A transient mid-response disconnect fails the fetch or probe even when the next attempt would succeed. — Fix: Include `http.client.IncompleteRead` in both bounded retry handlers and extend `test_returns_body`.
